Wecker} \maketitle egin{abstract}We study sparse graphs.\end{abstract} \section{Introduction}` | | 14.2 | Title block with affiliations and keywords | Write a paper's title block with two authors, each with a university affiliation, and a list of keywords. | ` itle{Deep Nets} \author[1]{Alice Smith} \author[2]{Bob Jones} \affil[1]{University of Oxford} \affil[2]{Stanford University} \maketitle extbf{Keywords:} graphs, networks, learning` | | 14.3 | Theorem and proof | Write a short mathematical passage with a numbered theorem followed by its proof, ending with an end-of-proof mark. | ` egin{theorem}There are infinitely many primes.\end{theorem} egin{proof}Suppose there are finitely many, $p_1,\dots,p_n$. Then $p_1\cdots p_n+1$ has a prime factor not in the list, a contradiction.\end{proof}` | | 14.4 | Numbered definition | Write a numbered definition of a prime number, set apart from the surrounding text the way math books do. | ` egin{definition}A \emph{prime number} is an integer $p>1$ whose only positive divisors are $1$ and $p$.\end{definition}` | | 14.5 | Epigraph | Write the opening of a chapter with a short epigraph quotation and its attribution, set apart before the first paragraph. | `\chapter{Beginnings} \epigraph{All happy families are alike.}{Leo Tolstoy} The morning was cold when we set out.` | | 14.6 | Pull quote | Write a paragraph of an article and a pull quote that repeats a striking line from it in larger type. | `The town had changed overnight. Nobody could say why the river ran backwards. \pullquote{Nobody could say why the river ran backwards.}` | | 14.7 | Framed box | Write a paragraph followed by a short piece of text inside a framed box. | `This paragraph introduces the idea. egin{tcolorbox}Remember: always back up your data.\end{tcolorbox}` | | 14.8 | Algorithm in pseudocode | Write a short algorithm in numbered pseudocode with the caption 'Binary search'. | ` egin{algorithm} \caption{Binary search} egin{algorithmic}[1] \State $lo \gets 0$, $hi \gets n-1$ \While{$lo \le hi$} \State $mid \gets \lfloor (lo+hi)/2 floor$ \If{$A[mid]=x$} \Return $mid$ \ElsIf{$A[mid] CO2 + 2H2O}` | | 14.16 | Margin to-do note | Write a paragraph with an editorial to-do note attached to it, shown in the margin. | `The results suggest a strong correlation. odo{Add a citation for this claim.}` | | 14.17 | Line numbers for review | Write a short paragraph set up so that the printed version shows line numbers in the margin for reviewers. | `\usepackage{lineno} \linenumbers This paragraph will be printed with line numbers in the margin so that reviewers can refer to specific lines.` | | 14.18 | Drop cap | Write the first paragraph of a story with its first letter set as a large drop cap. | `\lettrine{I}{t was} a dark and stormy night, and the wind howled across the moor.` | | 14.19 | Hyphenation hints | Write a sentence containing the word electroencephalography, marking the places where it may be hyphenated. | `The lab specializes in elec\-tro\-en\-ceph\-a\-log\-ra\-phy.` | | 14.20 | Numbered paragraphs | Write three paragraphs of a contract that are numbered 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 automatically. | ` egin{enumerate}[label=1.\arabic*] \item The Supplier shall deliver the goods. \item The Buyer shall pay within thirty days. \item Either party may terminate with notice. \end{enumerate}` | | 14.21 | Colored text | Write a sentence where the word 'blocked' is shown in red text. | `The deployment is extcolor{red}{blocked} until review is complete.` | | 14.22 | Subtext line | Write a heading followed by a line of small, muted subtext under it. | `\section{Project Overview} {\small\color{gray} Last updated March 2025}` | | 14.23 | Inline badge | Write a sentence ending with a small colored badge that reads 'beta'. | `This feature is still under development beta` | | 14.24 | Inline data fields | Write a note about a book that includes a rating of 5 and a genre of mystery as data fields a query tool could read. | `Finished reading *The Hound of the Baskervilles*. (rating:: 5) (genre:: mystery)` | | 14.25 | Key-value list | Write a short list of facts about a person (name, year born, occupation) that should display as aligned key-value pairs. | `/ Name: Ada Lovelace / Born: 1815 / Occupation: Mathematician` | | 14.26 | Side-brace grouping | Write three related lines grouped together by a large curly brace with a label beside it. | `$\left. egin{array}{l} ext{apples}\ ext{pears}\ ext{plums}\end{array} ight\}\ ext{fruit}$` | | 14.27 | Table formula | Write a small table of expenses whose total row is computed by a formula. | `#let e = (1000, 400, 150) #table(columns: 2, [Rent], [#e.at(0)], [Food], [#e.at(1)], [Travel], [#e.at(2)], [Total], [#e.sum()])` | | 14.28 | Callout on one list item | Write a bulleted list where one item is highlighted as a warning by a marker at the start of that item. | `- Install the package - [!WARNING] Back up your data first - Run the migration` | | 14.29 | Note template | Write a daily-note template that inserts today's date and the note's title automatically when a note is created. | `# <% tp.file.title %> Date: <% tp.date.now("YYYY-MM-DD") %> ## Tasks - [ ] ` | | 14.30 | Inline icon | Write a sentence with a small heart icon from an icon set shown inline. | `We aHeart{} open source software.` |
